candidates.name: Credo Technology
candidates.thesis: Q1 FY27 hypergrowth is now reinforced by a broader 1.6T optical platform: ZeroFlap combines Credo DSP, silicon photonics and PILOT telemetry, expanding the company from electrical interconnect toward an integrated AI-connectivity stack.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation, customer concentration and exceptionally high expectations remain the main risks.

candidates.name: Astera Labs
candidates.thesis: Astera is broadening from retimers and fabric switching into rack-scale memory connectivity; the new Leo family adds fabric-attached and pooled memory architectures and management reports broader hyperscaler design activity.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation, hyperscaler concentration and execution risk across several simultaneous product ramps.

candidates.name: Ciena
candidates.thesis: The optical-networking inflection is now supported by explicit FY2029 targets: roughly 30% revenue CAGR from FY26, ~50% adjusted gross margin, 32-35% adjusted operating margin and ~20% free-cash-flow margin.
candidates.risk: Customer concentration, supply constraints and a demanding multi-year execution path; valuation remains sensitive to any normalization in AI optical capex.

candidates.name: Lumentum Holdings
candidates.thesis: Optical connectivity remains a core AI-rack bottleneck with exceptional growth, margin expansion and strong forward guidance; ECOC activity reinforces the technology roadmap but does not change the earnings thesis this week.
candidates.risk: Extreme rerating increases valuation and drawdown risk; optical cycles can reverse sharply if capacity catches demand.

candidates.name: Celestica
candidates.thesis: AI data-center hardware growth remains exceptional, with no new thesis-changing fundamental datapoint this week.
candidates.risk: Customer concentration, equity dilution, lower structural margins than semiconductor IP businesses and execution risk on rapid expansion.

candidates.name: Broadcom
candidates.thesis: AI custom silicon and networking remain an exceptional earnings engine and a benchmark for moat quality, though mega-cap scale limits early-stage asymmetry.
candidates.risk: Mega-cap scale, premium expectations and customer concentration reduce discovery asymmetry.

candidates.name: Tower Semiconductor
candidates.thesis: Tower has moved from a diversified specialty foundry to a credible upstream AI-optics bottleneck: Q2 revenue grew 24%, SiPho reached a $680M annual run-rate from $180M a year earlier, management targets >$1B SiPho run-rate in Q4, and laser-integrated 800G/1.6T PICs are now shipping in volume with 6.4T planned for 1H27.
candidates.risk: Foundry capital intensity, execution on rapid SiPho capacity expansion, customer concentration and cyclicality in non-AI analog markets.

candidates.name: Arista Networks
candidates.thesis: AI-network demand and strong 2026 growth expectations remain intact; no thesis-changing company datapoint this week.
candidates.risk: Large-cap maturity, premium valuation and hyperscaler concentration reduce multibagger asymmetry.

candidates.name: Fabrinet
candidates.thesis: Advanced optical manufacturing continues benefiting directly from AI data-center optical demand and next-generation transceiver scaling.
candidates.risk: Customer concentration and outsourced-manufacturing economics; expectations have risen substantially.

candidates.name: Marvell Technology
candidates.thesis: Custom AI silicon, connectivity and electro-optics provide broad exposure to AI infrastructure, with strong bookings and raised multi-year outlooks.
candidates.risk: Hyperscaler concentration and long-dated custom-silicon expectations create execution and valuation risk.

candidates.name: Nebius Group
candidates.thesis: The Palantir sovereign-AI partnership remains strategically meaningful and demand visibility is strong, but this week adds no new primary fundamental evidence sufficient to raise the score further.
candidates.risk: The model remains extremely capital intensive with financing, customer concentration and execution risks.

candidates.name: Soitec
candidates.thesis: Silicon-photonics substrates remain an upstream AI-optics bottleneck with multi-year customer commitments supporting visibility.
candidates.risk: Sharp rerating, cyclical non-photonics end-markets and dependence on sustained hyperscaler optical adoption.

candidates.name: Onto Innovation
candidates.thesis: AI advanced packaging, HBM and silicon photonics continue driving process-control intensity; backlog above $1B supports visibility.
candidates.risk: Semiconductor equipment cyclicality, customer capex timing and premium expectations can produce large drawdowns.

candidates.name: Coherent Corp.
candidates.thesis: Broad photonics scale benefits from the copper-to-optics transition and continued AI datacenter optical capacity expansion.
candidates.risk: High capex raises execution and cycle risk if optical supply catches demand; broader portfolio dilutes pure-play AI exposure.

candidates.name: Snowflake
candidates.thesis: Product-revenue growth has reaccelerated while AI adoption and operating leverage improve, making Snowflake the radar's strongest enterprise-AI software candidate.
candidates.risk: Premium software valuation, stock-based compensation/GAAP losses and consumption-model variability remain material risks.

candidates.name: Camtek
candidates.thesis: Advanced-packaging inspection remains at an inflection as a large order book is expected to convert into accelerating H2 revenue and further growth in 2027.
candidates.risk: Current trailing growth remains below the forward order signal; semiconductor-capex timing and customer concentration create volatility.

candidates.name: Kulicke & Soffa Industries
candidates.thesis: Strong FY26 rebound plus CPO, HBM and advanced-packaging tooling exposure keep K&S on the agent-only watchlist, but no new thesis-changing evidence appeared this week.
candidates.risk: Historically cyclical semiconductor-equipment demand, product-ramp execution and uncertainty over how quickly CPO revenue becomes material.

candidates.name: Vertiv Holdings
candidates.thesis: Power and liquid-cooling infrastructure remain critical bottlenecks as AI rack density rises.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation and sensitivity to hyperscaler capex expectations; industrial capacity expansion can create cyclicality.

candidates.name: Amphenol
candidates.thesis: High-speed interconnect exposure is compounding with broad diversification and strong organic growth, orders and cash generation.
candidates.risk: Acquisition-driven reported growth and large-cap scale make it less asymmetric than smaller emerging compounders.

candidates.name: Arteris
candidates.thesis: Network-on-chip IP remains a small-cap picks-and-shovels exposure to increasingly complex AI chips and chiplets.
candidates.risk: Still loss-making, small revenue base and volatile licensing timing; design wins must convert into durable profitable growth.

candidates.name: GE Vernova
candidates.thesis: AI/data-center electricity demand reinforces a multi-year power and grid bottleneck, supported by strong orders and backlog.
candidates.risk: Strong rerating, long-cycle execution and project timing; not a pure-play AI growth company.
